content: The term hairy cell leukemia was first introduced to describe this malignancy by Dr. R. Schrek and Dr. W. J. Donnelly in 1966. The condition known as leukemic reticuloendotheliosis was initially described by Dr. O. Ewald, a German physician, in 1923. The first recognition of hairy cell leukemia as a distinct clinicopathological entity was reported by Dr. Bertha A. Bouroncle in 1958. The term hairy cell leukemia was officially coined by Dr. R. Schrek and Dr. W. J. Donnelly in 1966, as referenced in the work by Fanta PT and Saven A (2008), titled Hairy Cell Leukemia, published in Cancer Treatment and Research (Volume 142, Pages 193–209).
